protocols.title: Schauberger Water Vortexer (Wasserwirbler)
protocols.claim: A hyperbolic funnel with a narrow threaded (rifled) outlet generates a centripetal vortex in water that is claimed to cool it, 'revitalize'/densify it (claimed softer, rounder mouthfeel), reduce algae, and reduce irrigation energy by ~30%. Labeled a claim, not a finding.
protocols.objective: Home test of one measurable facet of the vortex-water claim (temperature, blind taste, or algae) as the archive's first independent data point on the Schauberger vortex lineage.
steps: Test A — temperature: fill two identical containers from one source bucket; pour one through the vortexer (full funnel pour, free spin) and one through a plain conical funnel as control at matching height/rate.
Measure both temps immediately and at 5, 15, 60 min with a 0.1°C thermometer; repeat N=5; note ambient temp.
Test B — blind taste: 3 cups per session (A, B, a second B) labeled randomly by a helper; tester ranks softer/rounder vs harder/flatter; 5+ sessions, score vs chance (binomial).
Test C — algae (2 weeks): two identical tanks, same water/light/source; tank B gets vortexed water changes; photograph daily, rank greenness blind.
Test D — irrigation (optional): two rows of identical seedlings; row B watered with vortexed water; measure water volume, growth, wilting days.
protocols.expected_outcome: Temperature: consistent ≥0.3°C difference (same direction ≥4/5 trials) supports claim facet 1; <0.1°C or random direction does not. Taste: ≥8/10 'softer/rounder' picks supports; ~5/10 is chance. Algae: tank B ranked less green ≥4/5 sessions supports.
protocols.safety: Trivial — water and plastic; nothing pressurized, nothing hot.

protocols.title: Eeman Relaxation Circuit (Blind Pulse Test)
protocols.claim: A coil of insulated copper wire laid out with head band and hand/foot contacts, connected to itself with NO power source, is claimed (by a 90-year-old tradition) to create a relaxed, coherent state when a person lies in the circuit. Honest framing: this is a claim the dossier exists to test against a sham.
protocols.objective: Controlled ~$10 blind test of ONE measurable facet: does lying in the closed circuit change resting pulse (parasympathetic tone) or self-rated relaxation vs a visually identical sham (wire cut)?
steps: Build two identical-looking mats: the circuit (coil in a figure-eight, connections joined, hand contacts wired to coil ends) and the sham (identical layout, one wire cut so it is not a closed circuit).
Recruit one tester + one helper; helper knows which is which, tester does not; label mats X and Y.
Tester lies still 10 min on mat X; helper measures pulse at 0, 5, 10 min; 10 min rest off-mat; then mat Y, same schedule; order randomized each session; 5+ sessions.
Record self-rated relaxation 0-10 before/after each (tester's blind rating).
Analyze pulse trend + relaxation delta, circuit vs sham; look for consistent difference (≥4/5 sessions same direction).
protocols.expected_outcome: Circuit consistently lower resting pulse / higher relaxation delta vs sham (≥4/5 blind sessions, delta ≥3 bpm or ≥2/10 relaxation points) → measurable effect. No consistent difference → classic $10 negative; still a win as an honest data point.
protocols.safety: Trivial — no power, no heat, no electricity.

protocols.title: Tesla Radiant Energy Receiver
protocols.claim: Tesla's patents (US 685,957 / 685,958, 1901) assert an elevated insulated conducting plate connected through a capacitor to ground accumulates charge from the environment ('radiant energy'), day and night. Honest framings: known 2026 physics predicts SOME collection (atmospheric potential gradient, RF, triboelectric); the test measures magnitude vs a shielded control, not 'is atmospheric electricity real'. Expected magnitude is micro-watts — enough to move a meter, not to power a household.
protocols.objective: Control test of how much charge a home-built elevated-plate receiver actually collects, above a shielded (Faraday) control.
steps: Mount the plate atop an insulating pole at 3-5 m in the open; run insulated downlead to the film capacitor's high terminal; capacitor's other terminal to ground.
Place DMM across the capacitor (10 MΩ bleeds continuously — that is the load); record.
Session: measure voltage at 0, 5, 10, 15 min; note weather, sky, time of day; run 5+ sessions across varied conditions (never in storms).
Control (same session, alternating): wrap the plate in grounded aluminum foil (Faraday shield); same schedule; control should read ~0.
Log every number: date, time, sky, wind, V at each interval, control V.
protocols.expected_outcome: Receiver accumulates charge consistently above the shielded control (≥10× control noise, same direction ≥4/5 sessions) → collection confirmed, mechanism unresolved; report honest micro-watt scale. No accumulation above control → does not replicate at home scale under fair conditions.
protocols.safety: No mains connection anywhere. The elevated conductor is a lightning attractant — disconnect and ground the antenna when storms are near or when unattended. Fair-weather instrument only; never run in thunderstorms.

protocols.title: Walter Schauberger Hyperbolic Funnel Vortex
protocols.claim: A clear hyperbolic funnel induces stable free-surface hyperbolic water vortices (Walter Schauberger 1960s design); a peer-reviewed JoVE protocol (2023) reports the vortex achieves oxygen transfer rates (SOTR) exceeding comparable aeration systems, with energy-efficient operation. The SOTR performance is a published claim, not a finding confirmed in this archive.
protocols.objective: Reproduce the JoVE protocol: produce a stable free-surface hyperbolic vortex, observe flow regimes, and measure dissolved-oxygen transfer (SOTR) vs a control.
steps: Position a clear hyperbolic funnel (10-15 cm upper, 1-2 cm outlet, 20-30 cm tall, y=k/x profile) vertically over a 20-50 L reservoir.
Connect a submersible pump (5-10 W, 1-5 L/min) as bottom feed or pour from the top; adjust flow to establish a vortex.
Fill reservoir with dechlorinated water at known temperature; record initial dissolved oxygen (DO).
Start pump, establish stable vortex, run 30 min; record final DO; calculate SOTR = (DO_final - DO_initial) × volume / time.
Document which of the three flow regimes forms (A: smooth; B: visible vortex core + air entrainment; C: deep air core, turbulent).
protocols.expected_outcome: PASS: SOTR exceeds 2× a comparable bubble diffuser at the same power, a stable vortex forms within 60 s, and two or more regimes are observable. FAIL: no stable vortex, SOTR at/below control, or funnel not hyperbolic. INCONCLUSIVE: marginal SOTR (1.2-1.9×), missing equipment, or single run only.
protocols.safety: Trivial — water and glass/acrylic; secure the funnel to avoid spills.

protocols.title: Blind Geopathic Zone Mapping (Inter-Rater Dowsing Test)
protocols.claim: Radiesthesia/dowsing practitioners claim 'geopathic stress zones' (Hartmann / Curry earth-energy lines) can be located in a home with simple L-rods. Honest status: contested — the best-known controlled test (Kassel 1991, analyzed by J.T. Enright) found skilled dowsers at chance when blinded; the Furter UZH dissertation reports only tendencies, not significance. This protocol is designed so the claim can pass OR fail cleanly.
protocols.objective: Test whether two people mapping the same room independently, blind to each other, agree on line positions above the chance baseline (cross-room control).
steps: Build two L-rod sets (metal coat hangers/welding rod, long arm ~30 cm, handle ~10 cm; straw over the handle lets the rod swing freely).
Two mappers who have not discussed the room; a third witness/referee coordinates; mappers never see each other's maps or floor marks.
Room 1 (test): each mapper walks the room recording (x, y) positions where the rods cross/swing/dip; maps go to the referee; floor marks removed before the next mapper enters.
Room 2 (control): both repeat in a different room under the same blind conditions.
Repeat at least 3 sessions on different days; referee scores same-room agreement (30 cm match rule) vs cross-room chance baseline.
protocols.expected_outcome: PASS (supports for this home/mappers): same-room agreement ≥70% on average AND clearly exceeds cross-room chance by ≥25 percentage points. FAIL: same-room within 10 points of chance. INCONCLUSIVE: above chance but below 70%, fewer than 3 sessions, or only one mapper (solo mapping counts as nothing).
protocols.safety: Trivial — no devices, no electricity, no physical influence; a fully honest test of inter-rater agreement.

equipment.name: Hyperbolic funnel
equipment.specs: Clear acrylic or glass following a hyperbolic profile: upper 10-15 cm, outlet 1-2 cm, height 20-30 cm, curve y=k/x. DIY alternative: plastic mixing bowl with a drilled outlet or a grain/feed funnel (closer to hyperbolic than a conical kitchen funnel).

equipment.name: Conical kitchen funnel (control)
equipment.specs: Standard conical kitchen funnel used as the pour-height/rate-matched control in the wasserwirbler temperature test, and as the control shape in the hyperbolic-funnel-vortex comparison.

equipment.name: Threaded / rifled narrow outlet
equipment.specs: A PVC or brass pipe nipple with visible rifling/threads at the vortexer outlet (the claimed twist mechanism), e.g. a 1/2" threaded nipple in a 3/4→3/8 reducer.

equipment.name: Kitchen thermometer (0.1°C)
equipment.specs: Calibrated digital kitchen thermometer with 0.1°C resolution if possible; used for water temperature differentials and reservoir temperature logging.

equipment.name: Two identical water containers
equipment.specs: Two matching containers for source-vs-treated comparison; identical so volume and pour geometry are matched.

equipment.name: Insulated copper wire coil
equipment.specs: 5-10 m of insulated copper wire (~0.5-1 mm²; hookup wire works), laid in a figure-eight on flexible foam/board with hand/foot contact loops. No power source.

equipment.name: Hand/foot contact pads
equipment.specs: Two flat metal/foil contact pads (or bare-wire loops) for the hands wired to the coil ends of the Eeman circuit.

equipment.name: Pulse monitor
equipment.specs: Fingers + a phone timer, or a cheap pulse oximeter / HRV app for a cleaner resting-pulse signal.

equipment.name: Elevated insulated conducting plate
equipment.specs: Aluminum or galvanized steel plate ~30×30 cm (or a 5-10 m horizontal wire antenna) mounted on insulating supports at 3-5 m, connected via insulated downlead to the capacitor.

equipment.name: Wooden / fiberglass pole (insulating)
equipment.specs: Wooden or fiberglass pole 3-5 m. Must NOT be metal — the collector must stay insulated from ground.

equipment.name: Low-leakage film capacitor
equipment.specs: Polypropylene film capacitor, 10-100 nF. NOT electrolytic — leakage ruins the charge-accumulation test.

equipment.name: Ground connection
equipment.specs: Ground rod preferred; clamp to a metal cold-water pipe as fallback. Common return for the elevated-plate receiver.

equipment.name: Digital multimeter (10 MΩ input)
equipment.specs: Digital multimeter with 10 MΩ input impedance (most DMMs; check the spec sheet) for DC voltage across the capacitor.

equipment.name: Aluminum foil Faraday shield (control)
equipment.specs: Heavy aluminum foil wrapped around the plate and connected to ground for the shielded-control noise floor; the control should read ~0.

equipment.name: Water reservoir (20-50 L)
equipment.specs: 20-50 L container of dechlorinated water at known temperature for the hyperbolic-funnel vortex test.

equipment.name: Submersible pump
equipment.specs: Submersible pump, 5-10 W, flow adjustable 1-5 L/min; vinyl tubing ~1 cm diameter. Bottom-feeds the hyperbolic funnel to establish the vortex.

equipment.name: Dissolved oxygen meter
equipment.specs: For dissolved-oxygen readings before/after the funnel-vortex run; used to compute oxygen transfer rate (SOTR).

equipment.name: Two L-rod sets
equipment.specs: Metal coat hangers or welding rod bent into an L (long arm ~30 cm, handle ~10 cm), one set per mapper; a drinking straw over the handle lets the rod swing freely.

equipment.name: Tape measure
equipment.specs: One per mapper (or two) to record (x, y) map positions from two fixed walls.

equipment.name: Graph paper + pencils
equipment.specs: One sheet per mapper per room; also painter's tape (optional) for floor marking that must be removed before the next mapper enters.

variables.name: Water temperature (vortexed vs control)
variables.measurement_procedure: Fill two identical containers from the same source bucket; pour one through the vortexer and one through a plain conical funnel at matching height/rate; measure immediately and at 5, 15, 60 min with a 0.1°C thermometer; repeat N=5 and note ambient temp.
variables.confounds: Ambient drift, pour height/rate mismatch, thermometer resolution, evaporation

variables.name: Blind mouthfeel preference
variables.measurement_procedure: 3 cups per session (A, B, a second B) labeled randomly by a helper who is not the tester; tester picks 'softer/rounder' vs 'harder/flatter'; 5+ sessions score vs chance (binomial).
variables.typical_range: Claim threshold: ≥8/10 selections of the vortexed cup; ~5/10 is chance
variables.confounds: Expectation bias (mitigated by blinding), cup/volume difference, taster discrimination

variables.name: Algae growth (ranked photos)
variables.measurement_procedure: Two identical small tanks, same water/light/algae source (a spoon of pond water each); one gets vortexed water changes; photograph daily and rank greenness blind.
variables.typical_range: 2-week observation; claim supported if tank B ranked less green ≥4/5 sessions
variables.confounds: Light/position differences, algae-source heterogeneity, photo exposure

variables.name: Irrigation water volume + seedling growth
variables.measurement_procedure: Two rows of identical seedlings, same soil; measure water volume used, growth (height), and wilting days weekly with photos.
variables.typical_range: Claim threshold: ≥20% water-volume reduction at equal growth

variables.name: Resting pulse
variables.measurement_procedure: Helper measures pulse at 0, 5, 10 min while the tester lies in the circuit vs the sham mat; order randomized each session; 5+ sessions.
variables.typical_range: Claim threshold: delta ≥3 bpm, same direction ≥4/5 sessions
variables.confounds: Order/carryover, time-of-day arousal, tester awareness (blinded), measurement error

variables.name: Self-rated relaxation
variables.measurement_procedure: Tester rates relaxation 0-10 before/after each mat session (their own blind rating).
variables.typical_range: Claim threshold: delta ≥2/10 points vs sham, same direction ≥4/5

variables.name: Capacitor accumulated voltage
variables.measurement_procedure: DMM across the film capacitor at 0, 5, 10, 15 min in each session, alternating with the grounded-foil shielded control; record weather/sky/time.
variables.typical_range: Micro-watt scale at home (½CV²); receiver should be ≥10× control noise, same direction ≥4/5 sessions
variables.confounds: Atmospheric gradient, RF rectification, triboelectric, humidity/weather, leaky capacitor

variables.name: Charge accumulation rate
variables.measurement_procedure: Derived from the per-interval voltage record over each session; compared directly against the shielded-control rate.
variables.typical_range: Receiver rate should exceed control rate ≥10× (fair-weather conditions only)
variables.confounds: Same as charge-voltage; session-to-session weather variability

variables.name: Vortex shape and stability
variables.measurement_procedure: Document which of the three regimes forms by adjusting flow (A smooth, B visible vortex core + air entrainment, C deep air core/turbulent); pass requires a stable vortex within 60 s.
variables.typical_range: At least 2 regimes observable; stable vortex within 60 s
variables.confounds: Funnel geometry mismatch, pump flow stability, reservoir setup

variables.name: Flow rate
variables.measurement_procedure: Set/measure pump flow (1-5 L/min) with a measuring cup + stopwatch; correlate with vortex regime.
variables.confounds: Pump calibration, tubing resistance, head height

variables.name: Dissolved oxygen / oxygen transfer (SOTR)
variables.measurement_procedure: Record initial and final DO over a 30-min vortex run; SOTR = (DO_final - DO_initial) × volume / time; compare to a bubble-diffuser control at the same power.
variables.confounds: Initial DO, water temp, reservoir volume, run time, control power

variables.name: Inter-rater agreement (same-room vs chance)
variables.measurement_procedure: Referee overlays Mapper A's and Mapper B's maps for the same room; a match is a marked position within 30 cm of the other's; agreement % = matched ÷ total. Cross-room (different rooms) gives the chance baseline; 3+ sessions on different days.
variables.typical_range: PASS: same-room ≥70% AND ≥25 points above chance; FAIL: within 10 points of chance; else INCONCLUSIVE
variables.confounds: Shared bias (doorways/furniture), mapping precision, session day effects, only-one-mapper caveat
